article.title: The Curious Case of Mixed Content in XML
article.paragraph: XML allows elements to contain a mixture of text and child elements, known as mixed content. For example, Alan Turing proposed the Turing test in 1950, building on earlier work by Ada Lovelace.
Whitespace handling in mixed content is tricky: parsers preserve significant whitespace between text and tags, but the xml:space="preserve" attribute can override defaults.
Leading and trailing whitespace is preserved here as well as inside code blocks.
